title: Desk Rule — Which Hours the Included Support Hours of a Building Automation Service Plan Are Drawn Against First
content:
# Desk Rule — Which Hours the Included Support Hours of a Building Automation Service Plan Are Drawn Against First

**The rule.** On a plan under the Building Automation Service Plans, where the tier includes an on-site controls visit escalation and the building carries a maintenance agreement standing active, the included support hours are drawn first against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance, and whatever of the included hours then remains is drawn against the remote hours. Where the tier includes an on-site controls visit escalation and the building carries no maintenance agreement standing active, the included support hours are drawn first against the remote hours, and whatever of the included hours then remains is drawn against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance. In every other case the included support hours are drawn against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance and the remote hours in the proportion each bears to the two of them together, the two of them together being taken as one hour where they fall below it, the share so drawn against the on-site hours taken to two decimal places.

Whether the building carries a maintenance agreement standing active is read from the office's records of Preventive Maintenance Agreements at that building: an agreement written against that building and standing active. Whether the plan's tier includes an on-site controls visit escalation is the tier's own entitlement.

| Tier includes on-site controls visit escalation | Maintenance agreement at the building standing active | The included support hours are drawn |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | first against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance, the remainder against the remote hours |
| yes | no | first against the remote hours, the remainder against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance |
| no | either | against the on-site hours left after the visit allowance and the remote hours in the proportion each bears to the two of them together |

## Worked case (hypothetical)

A plan whose tier includes an on-site controls visit escalation, at a building carrying an agreement under the Preventive Maintenance Agreements standing active, shows 6 on-site hours left after the visit allowance and 6 remote hours, with 8 hours standing to the plan's credit. The 8 included hours go first against the 6 on-site hours, clearing them; the remaining 2 go against the remote hours, leaving 4 remote hours.

Had the same building carried no agreement standing active, the 8 included hours would have gone first against the 6 remote hours, clearing them, and the remaining 2 against the on-site hours, leaving 4 on-site hours.
